findings.body: `activeBatchIds` contains only batches represented in returned query rows, and this code signs that subset as `pinnedActuals`. For a valid April–July answer with transactions only in April and July, the new link therefore contains only those two pins—the branch's own fixture at `chat.service.test.ts:295-299` models exactly this. On opening, `AskDrillService.bindPins` queries every Actual period in the range and, at `ask-drill.service.ts:184`, refuses the context when May or June has an ingest batch but no signed pin. Thus a row marked drillable with real transactions can produce a link that always fails. Include the complete executed-window Actual pin set or make route completeness validation consistent with contributing pins, and add a route-level sparse-month test.
findings.title: Multi-period drill links omit zero-contribution month pins

findings.body: The new wiring proof supplies both the result rows and expected labels through `FakeExecutor` and `FakeNames` (`chat.service.test.ts:1679-1685`), while the frontend test separately mocks the Ask response. No Playwright flow against the running API and real database proves that scoped SAP names, budget fallback, bare-code fallback, complete disclosure accessibility, and unchanged row order survive the actual query-to-browser path. Under the required test-audit rule for user-facing Done-when items, these isolated unit/component tests are not sufficient end-to-end proof.
findings.title: Not done: An Ask answer by GL code shows its scoped SAP/MIS names

findings.body: The multi-period statement test injects a fabricated result and a fabricated `FakeNames` label, then asserts only the service's call and signed claims. The existing frontend test likewise mocks the response. There is no browser flow through a running API and real database proving that a saved/pinned statement re-run resolves the final-month outline and renders its number/name while an actual-only answer stays raw. This leaves Done-when item 2 proven only at isolated unit/component boundaries.
findings.title: Not done: A budget-backed statement answer shows pinned line numbers and names

findings.body: The added size-limit rule says an oversized row carries no amount, but the unchanged generic context description at lines 82–84 still says every row binds its exact-paise Actual, and C5a at lines 223–224 repeats that each row carries one. These requirements remain mutually exclusive despite the implementation's discriminated union. Explicitly exempt the C5d inert variant in both generic descriptions.
findings.title: Keep oversized context rows consistent in the confirmed spec

findings.body: The task table still assigns rendering drillable Actuals as buttons and proving inert cells make no request to GL-DRILL-PANEL. The current Ask panel consumes labels but never reads `AskResponse.drill`, so this branch alone does not complete Done-when item 6's user-visible interaction. Per the explicit task assignment, this remains a P2 later-task gap rather than a blocker attributed to this backend wiring task.
findings.title: Later: GL-DRILL-PANEL must consume the signed drill metadata
